newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 17.

text.p: Two Mexican crude shipping ports were closed on Friday as a new cold front hit the Gulf of Mexico, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its daily report 1000 local/1600 GMT.
The two ports have been closed four out of five days this week.
Pajaritos, under the jurisdiction of Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz state, reshut Thursday at 1330 local/1930 GMT but wind speeds were relaxing Friday morning, port officials told Reuters.

At Dos Bocas in Tabasco state, port officials said crude shipping was again halted after closing 1600 local/2200 GMT Thursday. Winds were reported steady at 45 km per hour and waves at between nine to 12 feet high.
The largest of Mexico's crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained open throughout the week for petroleum shipping through the week's high winds and waves.

Pajaritos ships an average 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude and Dos Bocas exports 300,000 bpd, according to the latest oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) statistics. Cayo Arcas ships an average 600,000 bpd.
Other Gulf of Mexico ports, Frontera, Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche and Progreso, were closed, the ministry's daily morning bulletin said.
Smaller boats were restricted from sailing in Tampico, El Mezquital, La Pesca, Alvarado, Nautla, Tuxpan, Veracruz, Cozumel, Salina Cruz and Puerto Penasco.
The report also warned against sailing in the Gulf of Mexico and the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of winds and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Strong convective activity causing lower temperatures and clouds with possible light rains along the coasts of Baja California, Sonora, Sinaloa, Nayarit, Jalisco and Colima where winds from north and northeast 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) with waves four to seven feet high.
Winds along the coasts of Guerrero, Oaxaca and Chiapas states from north and northeast at 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/ 17 to 22 miles per hour) with winds seven to 11 feet high.

A new moderate cold front extending from the U.S. coast to the central gulf region and merging with a mass of cold air moving southeast and lowering temperatures in north, center and northeast states. Winds in ther region from the north and notheast at 15 to 25 knots (28 to 47 km/17 to 28 miles per hour) with waves six to nine feet high.
Moderate convective activity along the coast of Honduras, winds from the northeast at 15 to 20 knots with waves four to six feet high.
